title: Justice, nearest to taqwa
hook: a thumb near the scale, and the verse that puts fairness next to mindfulness of Allah

segments.voice: Yesterday: rifq, gentleness as the how, not a softer what. Today, a virtue that sounds hard-edged, and the surprising company the Qur'an keeps it in.

Grapes go on one side of a market scale, a weight on the other, and a thumb hovers just above the pan. Nobody is watching the thumb. That's the whole drama of fairness: much of it happens where no one is checking. Surah al-Ma'idah gives justice an unexpected neighbor. Not courage. Not law. In Pickthall's translation: "Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty."
screen: `A THUMB ABOVE THE PAN.` → `NOBODY IS CHECKING.` → `DEAL JUSTLY, THAT IS NEARER.`

segments.voice: Pickthall says duty. In the Arabic of the verse it's taqwa: mindfulness of Allah, guarding yourself, keeping watch over what you do. English struggles to hold it in one word, so translators choose different ones. And what comes nearest to it? Not a long night of prayer. Not a fast. Dealing justly. The word for justice is 'adl, and its picture is a balance: two sides level, nothing tipped. So taqwa isn't only something on a prayer mat. It shows up at the counter, in how a bill gets split, in how a fight gets retold. Second, the sky and the scale. Surah al-Rahman, in paraphrase: He raised the heaven and set up the balance, so do not cheat the balance; keep the weight fair and don't make the measure short. Third, the home. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, speaks of people on pulpits of light near Allah. In paraphrase: those who are just in their judgments, with their families, and in whatever they're put in charge of. The parent dividing the last slice. The older sister picking teams. The manager handing out the good shifts. And the same verse in al-Ma'idah won't let dislike off the hook: hatred of a people must not push anyone away from justice. Day six hundred seventy-seven gave that a day of its own. Today's focus is closer: fairness as a way of being mindful of Allah, right where the thumb is.
screen: `TAQWA: PICKTHALL SAYS DUTY.` · `'ADL: A BALANCE HELD LEVEL.` · `THE SKY AND THE SCALE TOGETHER.` · `PULPITS OF LIGHT: JUST AT HOME.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you'll divide or decide today, time, chores, credit for a piece of work, the last of the food, and look at it like a scale: where's your thumb, and is your side quietly a little heavier? Level that one thing in your mind and see it sitting even. If you pray, you can hold the line from al-Ma'idah: deal justly, that is nearer to your duty.
Justice. 'Adl: a balance held level, at the market, at home and in judgment, and called in surah al-Ma'idah nearer to taqwa. Today's word.
Your line: nearest to taqwa. Fairness lives right where nobody is checking. Tomorrow, keeping the ties of kin.

howItsDone: Muslims read al-Ma'idah 5:8 as tying justice to taqwa, and the hadith of the just on pulpits of light extends fairness to judgments, families and anything a person is put in charge of.
